atoms.b: World War One began in 1914 and ended in ((++1918 2018)). It affected lots of countries throughout ((++the_world America)).

feedback.finish: Millions of soldiers from all over Europe died, including around 880,000 British troops.

instruction.text: When the war started, soldiers from all over the British Empire were called to help. Select the globe to learn more.

text: Over 3 million soldiers from across the British Empire served alongside the British Army during World War One!

atoms.b: Many countries in ((++Europe London)) had alliances with each other.
An alliance means that if one country was attacked, their allies would ((++protect ignore)) them.
This is the reason it became a “World War”, as so many ((++countries planets)) got involved.

instruction.text: During the war, soldiers mainly fought in long ditches dug into the ground called trenches. Drag the soldier to the trench to learn more.

feedback.end: Soldiers lived in these trenches and only climbed out when it was time to attack. These trenches were often very wet, muddy and full of rats.

instruction.text: What do you think the soldiers living in these trenches would experience? Select the three correct images.

feedback.end: The conditions in the trenches were horrible! Soldiers would often get sick and got very little sleep or food.
